title_en: Fire Safety Basics for a Shared Rented Flat
summary_en: Basic fire safety habits for a shared rented flat, and what actually counts as a fire-code violation.
body_en:
In a flat shared by several tenants, fire safety habits matter more, not less. A habit that's harmless alone can become dangerous once multiplied by several people, especially in a flat with more belongings than storage space.

The corridor outside your door

The common corridor outside HDB flats must keep a clear escape passage, generally understood as a minimum of 1.2 metres wide. Storing items like shoe racks, bicycles, or boxes along the corridor can obstruct this escape route and firefighting access, including dry risers and hose reels.

What's actually prohibited

  • Storing combustible materials — cardboard boxes, newspapers, stacks of old magazines — along the common corridor.
  • Blocking fire hose reels, dry riser cabinets, or any clearly marked fire safety equipment.
  • Obstructing the common corridor so it can't be used as an escape route in an emergency.

The penalty for ignoring it

SCDF can issue a Fire Hazard Abatement Notice, and a serious infringement can lead to a Notice of Offence carrying a composition fine of up to S$5,000. Town Councils can separately fine residents up to S$5,000 for breaching their own by-laws on corridor use.

Inside the flat itself

  • Don't overload a single power socket with multiple adapters and appliances — this is a common cause of electrical fires.
  • Keep a basic understanding of where the nearest staircase is, not just the lift, since lifts shouldn't be used during a fire.
  • Agree with flatmates on safe cooking habits, especially if anyone cooks late at night or leaves the stove unattended.
  • Know where the nearest fire extinguisher or hose reel is on your floor, even if you never need to use it.

None of this takes much effort day to day. It only matters on the one day you hope never comes.

General guidance, November 2026 — not legal advice. See scdf.gov.sg for current fire safety guidelines.
